summary: Algorithm-neutral wrapper for a 32-byte symmetric key or seed sealed to a recipient public key. Algorithm details live only in the suite specifications listed below.

reservedKeyKinds.reason: signature key; never a wrapper recipient

reservedKeyKinds.reason: signature key; never a wrapper recipient

fields.name: wrapperSuiteId
fields.rule: registered suite whose lifecycle allows the operation and whose purposes include the descriptor purpose

fields.name: scope
fields.rule: exactly the identifiers selected by the purpose scopeBitmap; lowercase RFC 4122 UUIDs

fields.name: memberKeyGeneration
fields.rule: positive when present; presence follows the purpose

fields.name: recipientFingerprint
fields.rule: computed by the suite fingerprint function over the authenticated recipient public key

fields.name: encodedSealedKeyPackage

contextEncoding.layout: ASCII(PLDNX2W1) || u16be(protocolVersion) || u16be(len) || ASCII(wrapperSuiteId) || u16be(purpose) || u16be(scopeBitmap) || UUID16 for each present scope in organization-vault-entry-grantOrRequest-agent-member order || u64be(resourceRevision) || u32be(wrappedKeyVersion) || u8(hasMemberKeyGeneration) [|| u32be(memberKeyGeneration)] || u16be(recipientKeyKind) || u32be(recipientKeyVersion) || recipientFingerprint[32] || u8(hasParentDescriptorHash) [|| parentDescriptorHash[32]]
contextEncoding.suiteBinding: wrapperSuiteId is part of the encoded context, so opening a package under any other suite id fails context verification

rules: The expected suite is the suite registered with the recipient public key in its authenticated key directory, never the wrapperSuiteId claimed by the envelope; a mismatch fails as recipient-mismatch.

The expected descriptor is built from authenticated request, Vault, Member, Agent and key state before opening; the context hash inside the opened package must equal the hash of that independent descriptor.
Implementations select a suite only from this registry at build time; there is no algorithm negotiation and no runtime registration.
Product code outside the crypto module handles only wrapperSuiteId, recipientKeyKind and opaque package bytes.
Every suite other than palladin-x25519-sealed-box-v1 must bind its suite id into its recipient fingerprint input.
A seal operation requires an active suite; an open operation requires an active or read-only suite; retired suites fail closed.
